title: Cap. 6 Arg. 8 open: Fathers testify that God withholds media and gifts by good pleasure
pass_a_gloss: Our last argument will be drawn from the testimonies of the Fathers, who freely confess that to certain people—and that from the good pleasure of the divine will—those means and gifts are not given by which they can believe in Christ and obtain salvation: which God would never omit to do, if, Christ's death being posited, the account of divine goodness, prudence, or justice required that those things already be supplied to all and each. Nor will we run through the Fathers one by one, but from them we will excerpt a few testimonies with which they had business against the Pelagians and Semi-Pelagians.
pass_b_english: Our last argument comes from the Fathers themselves. They freely grant that some people are not given the means and gifts by which they can believe in Christ and obtain salvation—and that this denial rests on the good pleasure of the divine will. God would never leave that undone if, once Christ's death is granted, divine goodness, prudence, or justice already required those means to be supplied to every person. We will not parade every Father in turn. We will take a few passages from those who fought the Pelagians and Semi-Pelagians.
source_text: Postremum nostrum argumentum petetur a testimoniis Patrum, qui ultro fatentur, quibusdam hominibus, idque ex beneplacito Divinae voluntatis, non dari ea media ac dona quibus in Christum credere et salutem obtinere queant: quod Deus nunquam facere praetermitteret, si posita Christi morte, ratio bonitatis, prudentiae aut justitiae Divinae id exigeret omnibus et singulis jam suppeditari. Neque Patres singulos percurremus, sed ex iis paucula testimonia excerpemus, quibus cum Pelagianis et Semipelagianis negotium fuit.
